Human support

Technology finds the opportunity. People help you take it.

Every automated answer is backed by mentors, volunteers and students who have walked the same path.

The support we offer

Online mentoring

One-to-one sessions with students and volunteers who help you choose a pathway and plan the next steps.

Educational webinars

Live sessions on scholarships, university applications, Ausbildung and studying in Germany.

Question & answer sessions

Open sessions where you can ask anything about applications, documents, deadlines and recognition.

WhatsApp & Telegram groups

Daily opportunity updates and a place to ask short questions and get quick answers.

Student & volunteer guidance

Peer support from people who applied recently and know the process from the inside.

Planning your future

Structured support for people who know they want to study or train, but not yet what or where.

Get involved

Become a volunteer mentor

Are you a student, a graduate or a professional? A single hour per month is enough to change the direction of someone’s education. We especially welcome mentors who speak Dari, Pashto or Arabic.

Write to us

Response time

The AI assistant answers immediately, 24/7. A human reply usually takes one to three days — we are two students doing this next to our studies.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

The questions we receive most often — in every language we support.

No. All information, guidance, mentoring and tools are free. FEA is a non-profit initiative and does not charge fees, sell data or run advertising.

No. You can use the opportunity directory, the AI Analyzer and the chat without registering. Your analyzer answers stay in your own browser.

No. We do not submit applications and we are not an agency. We explain the requirements, help you understand the process and answer your questions — the application itself always stays yours.

Yes. A large part of our work is aimed at students in Afghanistan, especially girls and women. Many opportunities we list — online courses, language programmes and international scholarships — can be started from home.

An Ausbildung is a paid vocational training programme in Germany that combines working in a company with vocational school. It usually lasts two to three and a half years and ends with a recognised professional qualification.

It depends on the pathway. Ausbildung usually requires B1 to B2, a German-language degree programme usually requires C1, and many Master programmes are taught in English. Language courses and online courses are open at every level.

German, English, Dari and Arabic — on the website, in the chat and in our social media channels.

Every entry links to an official source such as DAAD, BAMF, the Bundesagentur für Arbeit or a university. We check entries regularly, but deadlines change — always confirm on the official page before applying.
